title: Mittag-Leffler vanishing under the tensor of a quotient-product map
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M$ a Mittag-Leffler $R$-module [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module], $E$ an $R$-module, $J$ any set, and $(N_j)_{j\in J}$ a family of submodules of $E$. Put $P=\prod_{j\in J}E/N_j$, the module of all families with componentwise operations, and let $q:E\to P$ send $e$ to $(e+N_j)_j$. Tensor products and induced tensor maps are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. The linear map $\beta:P\otimes_R M\to\prod_{j\in J}((E/N_j)\otimes_R M)$ defined on pure tensors by $\beta((a_j)_j\otimes m)=(a_j\otimes m)_j$ is injective. For every $x\in E\otimes_R M$, if $x$ belongs to the image of $N_j\otimes_R M\to E\otimes_R M$ induced by inclusion for every $j\in J$, then $(q\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(x)=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AS6 (lemma-minimal-contains), proof: the two displayed quotient-product maps and the implication between their zero images (returned Steps 2 and 3); no flatness is assumed in this auxiliary.

proof.text: For any $R$-modules $A,B$, write $s_{A,B}:A\otimes_R B\to B\otimes_R A$ for the $R$-linear isomorphism $\tau_{A,B}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-comm], so $s_{A,B}(a\otimes b)=b\otimes a$. Its inverse is $s_{B,A}$: the composites $s_{B,A}s_{A,B}$ and $s_{A,B}s_{B,A}$ fix every pure tensor, hence are identities because pure tensors generate [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. This supplies the change of tensor order needed below.

source.place: Tag 0AS6 (lemma-minimal-contains), tensor order in the two displayed quotient-product maps; symmetry of the tensor product (Tag 00CX universal property)

proof.text: Put $Q_j=E/N_j$. The Mittag-Leffler definition [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module], applied to this family, makes $\theta:M\otimes_R P\to\prod_j(M\otimes_R Q_j)$ injective. The map $((a_j)_j,m)\mapsto(a_j\otimes m)_j$ is bilinear componentwise, so the tensor universal property defines $\beta$. On a generator $a\otimes m$, with $a=(a_j)_j$, both $(\prod_j s_{M,Q_j})\theta s_{P,M}$ and $\beta$ give $(a_j\otimes m)_j$; hence they agree on the entire tensor product. The product of the swaps has inverse the componentwise product of their inverses, and $s_{P,M}$ is invertible by Step 1. Since $\theta$ is injective, this factorization proves injectivity of $\beta$.

source.place: Tag 059M (proposition-ML-tensor), condition (2); Tag 0AS6 (lemma-minimal-contains), implication between the two displayed maps

proof.text: Write $\pi_j:P\to Q_j$ for projection, $p_j:E\to Q_j$ for the quotient map and $i_j:N_j\hookrightarrow E$ for inclusion. Then $\pi_jq=p_j$ and $p_ji_j=0$. On each pure tensor $e\otimes m$, the $j$th coordinate of $\beta(q\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)$ equals $(e+N_j)\otimes m$, so that coordinate map is $p_j\otimes\mathrm{id}_M$ by generation. Fix $j$ and choose $y_j\in N_j\otimes_R M$ mapping to $x$, as the hypothesis permits. Tensor functoriality gives $(p_j\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(x)=((p_ji_j)\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(y_j)=0$. Thus every coordinate of $\beta((q\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(x))$ is zero. By Step 2 and $\beta(0)=0$, injectivity gives $(q\otimes\mathrm{id}_M)(x)=0$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q63-692a02296 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read all three steps, both cited definitions and Stacks algebra.tex lemma-minimal-contains (Tag 0AS6, line 21534) together with Tag 059M; tags/tags confirms both labels. The item isolates the step of the Stacks proof where zero in ∏(F/F_i⊗M) gives zero in (∏F/F_i)⊗M. It states this without flatness and phrases the hypothesis as 'x is in the image of each N_j⊗M'. That is correct and not a weakening: the parent lem-trf-flat-ml-minimal-support uses it in its Step 2 with exactly the same P and q, and adds flatness only in its Step 3. Step 2: checked β = (∏ swaps)∘θ∘swap on generators; θ is injective by def-trf-mittag-leffler-module (M on the left). Step 3: p_j i_j = 0 and the j-th coordinate of β(q⊗id) is p_j⊗id, so each j needs only its own lift and no compatible lifts. Edge cases tested: J empty, J a singleton, all N_j = E, some N_j = 0, the non-flat M = Z/2 over Z, and the zero ring. No re-split note applies, there are no new nodes and no SGA citations. One fix (C5): Step 1 re-derived tensor symmetry from the universal property, but the DAG already has the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-module-tensor-comm (TensorProduct.comm). Step 1 now cites that leaf for the swap, and Steps 1–2 uses and proof_deps include it. It is a Mathlib leaf, so it adds no cycle and needs no tool_use.
